{{Use list-defined references|date=April 2021}}
'''Gordana Todorov''' (born July 24, 1949){{r|born}} is a mathematician working in [[noncommutative algebra]], [[representation theory]], [[Artin algebra]]s, and [[cluster algebra]]s. She is a professor of mathematics at [[Northeastern University]].{{r|profile}}

== Biography ==
Todorov earned her Ph.D. in 1978, at [[Brandeis University]]. Her dissertation, ''Almost Split Sequences in the Representation Theory of Certain Classes of Artin Algebras'', was supervised by [[Maurice Auslander]].{{r|mg}}

Todorov is married to mathematician [[Kiyoshi Igusa]].{{r|kiyoshi}} The Igusa–Todorov functions{{r|functions}} and Igusa–Todorov endomorphism algebras{{r|algebra}} are named for their joint work. Todorov is also the namesake of Todorov's theorem on preprojective partitions,{{r|theorem}} and the Gentle–Todorov theorem on [[abelian category|abelian categories]].{{r|gentle}}
